messages.subject: Re: R squared of regression in measurement system
parts:
library(lavaan)
model <- '
# measurement model
ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
dem65 =~ y5 + y6 + y7 + y8
# regressions
dem60 ~ ind60
dem65 ~ ind60 + dem60
# residual correlations
y1 ~~ y5
y2 ~~ y4 + y6
y3 ~~ y7
y4 ~~ y8
y6 ~~ y8'

fit <- sem(model, data = PoliticalDemocracy)

summary(fit, rsquare = TRUE)                # Option 1
parameterEstimates(fit, rsquare = TRUE)     # Option 2
lavInspect(fit, "rsquare")                  # Option 3

messages.subject: Re: R squared of regression in measurement system
parts:
Sort of. R^2 is the proportion of the variance explained by the predictors. It says something about the predictive quality of the model and - just to have mentioned it - not about the fit of the model to the data (these are the fitMeasures). By the way, you can easily calculate R^2 yourself:

1 - lavInspect(fit, "est")$psi["dem60", "dem60"] / lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv")["dem60", "dem60"]
1 - lavInspect(fit, "est")$psi["dem65", "dem65"] / lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv")["dem65", "dem65"]
